### Findings

| Finding | Raised by | Severity | What and where | Closed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7.1 | PINV-1 | safety | Continues 6.1 (5.4). Parts rated 250 V on nets that reach 253 V rms (358 V peak): F101 (LINE_IN, LINE_F), F701 (COFFPUMP, PUMP_C_MT2), F711 (STEAMPUMP, PUMP_S_MT2), F731 (VALVE_COM), type code 250 V, holders 250 V AC; K731 and K741 (COFVALVE, HOTVALVE, VALVE_COM), maximum switching voltage 250 VAC. The SETfuse sheet prints breaking capacity at 300 VAC but states no 253 V use. Mains entry, Pump drives and Valve drives sheets. Owner decision: acceptance (c) names K731 and K741 and (c2) names F101, F701, F711 and F731 against the 253 V top of the span (about 1 %), bounded by the usual margin on 230 V and 240 V mains and firmware voltage monitoring, ground: the machine's other factory parts are rated 250 V; it covers this finding (signed entries for these six positions are in derating-policy.yaml). |  |
| 7.2 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.2. Pump drives sheet: (a) PUMP_C_MT2 and PUMP_S_MT2 (T701.2, T711.2) and the opto-triac terminals PUMP_C_OPTO_MT and PUMP_S_OPTO_MT (U701.6, U711.6): the voltage at turn-off on the inductive pump coil with no snubber and no clamp is in no record (716 V undamped estimate against VDRM 600 V, a repetitive rating); (b) new: PUMP_C_GATE_R and PUMP_S_GATE_R: each 200 ohm 1206 gate resistor stands about 180 V peak at each re-fire against a rated continuous working voltage of 7.07 V and an overload voltage of 17.7 V (UNI-ROYAL data sheet V.3 section 9 formula), with no pulse rating in the sheet. Owner decision: acceptance (d) names the not-fitted snubbers bounded by the bring-up measurement of the turn-off voltage at TP702 and TP712, and (g) a mains surge above the triacs' rating; they cover part (a) as the owner's accepted residual with the measurement carried to bring-up; no acceptance names the gate-resistor pulse voltage of part (b) ((i) names only a bridged resistor), so they do not cover part (b). |  |
| 7.3 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.3 (5.2). Controller sheet, USB_DM and USB_DP (D401 pins 1, 3, 4, 6 to J402 and U401 PA11 pin 70, PA12 pin 71): USBLC6-2SC6 lets 17 V through at 5 A (DS4260 Rev 7 Table 2; about 23 V at 24 A with D402 on VBUS, circuit-proof.md B surge row) to pins limited to 6 V (4.0 V with VDD absent) with no pulse withstand stated (DS12110 Rev 11 Table 109, Table 110). The record still carries the row as NO; there is no series resistor or lower-residue clamp. Owner decision: acceptance (f) names the USB data pins PA11 and PA12 behind D401, the 17 V at 5 A residue against the 6.0 V pin maximum, ground AN4879 arrangement, bounded by that arrangement and R403 C419; it covers this finding for the 17 V at 5 A residue; it does not state the 23 V at 24 A figure, which is not covered. |  |
| 7.4 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.4. Logic supply sheet, /Logic supply/+3V3_REG (U302 pin 3, JP302), VREF+ (U401 pin 20 via R302) and /Logic supply/+3V3A_FB (FB301, R301 to VDDA pin 21), and through JP302 every pin on +3V3 (U401 VDD pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100 and VBAT pin 6, U402, U601, U620, U621, U630, U631, Y601): a U302 failed short IN to OUT, or the module trip with the LDO conducting, puts 5.125 V to 6.75 V (10.3 V surge in the cable position) on a rail whose parts have 4.0 V absolute maximum (DS12110 Rev 11 Table 109; MAX31865 19-6478 Rev 3 4.0 V). Nothing clamps or crowbars +3V3; circuit-verdicts.md U302 row records it owner-held. Owner decision: acceptance (k) names the +3V3 rail after a regulator short and the +5V module trip, ground the regulating part failing short with damage confined to low-voltage logic, bounded by the interlock failing safe (a dead controller stops refreshing K201); it covers this finding (the 10.3 V cable-position level is the same input-rail-passed case). |  |
| 7.5 | PINV-1 | function | Flow, pressure and spare analogue inputs and Controller: FLOW_F, FLOW_IN (R522 0603 zero-ohm link from FLOW_F to FLOW_IN across U520; U401 pin 63 PC6, FT_h). Continues 6.6 (and 6.15, 6.73). The records now say U520 and C521 are fitted and R522 is not (circuit-verdicts.md R522 row, parts-specification.yaml), but sheet 52 and the netlist still draw and list R522 (value 0, `dnp no`, LCSC C21189) in parallel with U520, so the committed schematic joins the meter output to PC6 through R521 1 kohm and the link; the not-fitted state exists only as a board-footprint flag the schematic does not carry. With the link fitted and +3V3 absent a push-pull output of up to 5.25 V exceeds the 4.0 V pin limit (DS12110 Rev 11 Table 11) and Table 12 allows +0 mA injection that no series resistor meets. Would close: R522 removed from the schematic or marked do-not-populate in the sheet, so the circuit as committed is the one the records judge. Owner decision: none of acceptances (a) to (p) names this risk; it is not covered. |  |
| 7.6 | PINV-1 | function | Flow, pressure and spare analogue inputs and Current sensing inputs: nets BREW_AN (U401 PA6), SPARE_AN2 (PA0), STMP_AN (PC5), CURR1_AN (PA2), CURR2_AN (PA3) and FLOW_F (U520 pin 2). New in this form. The records bound the sensor output at 5.5 V (3.70 V at the pins, limit 4.0 V), but the +5V supply a sensor runs from can reach 6.75 V at the IRM-20 over-voltage trip (IRM-20-SPEC 2025-11-21: 5.75 to 6.75 V); an output that follows its supply gives 6.75 x 0.6731 = 4.54 V on the ADC pins (DS12110 Rev 11 Table 11 note 5, 4.0 V; 4.09 V even for a 0.5 to 4.5 V ratiometric output at 90 % of the rail) and 6.75 V on U520 pin 2 against its 6.5 V maximum (SCES351Y 5.1), where D520 (VBR 6 to 10 V) is not guaranteed to clamp. Would close: a lower divider ratio or clamp for the 6.75 V case, or the record bound moved to the trip level. Owner decision: acceptance (k) names the +5V module trip at 5.75 to 6.75 V and its bounding element (harm limited to low-voltage logic, the interlock fails safe), ground first boards of a five-board minimum order; it covers this finding, because the state is the one it names and the harm lands on controller and buffer pins, with no mains route (its stated cause, a regulating part failing short, is the same excursion). |  |
| 7.7 | PINV-1 | function | Flow, pressure and spare analogue inputs: BREWA_3V3, SPAREA_3V3, SPAN2_3V3 (J523, J524, J525 pin 2) and through them +3V3 and +3V3A (G6 rows on +3V3 and U401 VDD, VDDA). Continues 6.70. Each analogue header carries +5V on pin 1 and the 3.3 V feed on pin 2 beside it. A cable fault bridging them drives the feed through the link (R542 to R544) and the PTC (F522 to F524, 1.35 to 8.5 ohm, 0.2 s to trip at 1.0 A) into +3V3; the LT1963A cannot sink current (data sheet, no reverse current) and the rail load is about 37 mA, so the current falls as the rail rises toward about 5 V and stays below the PTC hold current, the PTC does not trip, and U401 VDD and VDDA (4.0 V maximum, DS12110 Rev 11 Table 11) stay over their maximum. No record examines this short and nothing clamps +3V3. Would close: reorder the header pins so a 3.3 V pin is not beside +5V, or a clamp or crowbar on +3V3. Owner decision: acceptance (k) names the +3V3 rail after a regulator short and its bounding element (harm limited to low-voltage logic); it does not cover this finding because the cause here is a cable or sensor fault on a connector that no regulator failure is involved in, and its ground is the regulating part failing short. |  |
| 7.8 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.7 (5.3). HX711 U630 and U631, Load-cell amplifiers sheet, nets WT1_INA_N, WT1_INA_P, WT1_VBG, WT1_CLK, WT1_DATA, WT2_INA_N, WT2_INA_P, WT2_VBG, WT2_CLK, WT2_DATA: the Avia V2.0 sheet (8 pages; re-read, and the 9-page LCSC-hosted copy of C6705483 holds the same text, also served by SparkFun at the same size) states a supply range 2.6 to 5.5 V and a common-mode input range, and no absolute maximum for any pin, no digital levels (VIH, VIL, VOH, VOL) and no tolerance with a supply absent. VSUP and AVDD sit on +5V, which the IRM-20 over-voltage trip (5.75 to 6.75 V, IRM-20-SPEC 2025-11-21) and the USB cable position (10.3 V at the D402 clamp, open-items.md M1) take above the only voltage the sheet states; circuit-proof.md still reads "Cannot be shown: there is no figure" for the +5V over-voltage row and marks E4.4 (levels) FAILS; open-items.md M1 carries a worst case assumed, not a rating. Owner decision: acceptance (k) names rail over-voltage fault states, the +5V module trip at 5.75 to 6.75 V and the load-cell 5 V rails among them (findings 6.3, 6.4, 6.7, 6.9, 6.10), bounded by the harm staying in low-voltage logic with K201 failing safe, ground the regulating part failing short; it covers this finding for the module-trip state; it does not cover this finding for the cable-position surge to 10.3 V (acceptance (b) names only U201 and U791, ground a bench state with mains off) nor for the missing digital levels, which are not a fault state. |  |
| 7.9 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.8. AMC131M02 AIN1P (U601 pin 8) on /Supply voltage and current measurement/AMC_AIN1P (R607 330 ohm, C602, TP604), Supply voltage and current measurement sheet. A shunt fault of 6 kA x 1 mohm = 6.00 V prospective (circuit-proof.md E1.7) takes the pin outside HGND-1.6 V to HGND+2.7 V (SBASA56 6.1). The record divides by 660 ohm (R607 and R608), but AIN1N sits at HGND, the same terminal as the shunt's neutral side (netlist R105 pin 3 SHUNT_SENSE_NEUTRAL and pin 4 NEUTRAL, and NT601 to AMC_HGND), so the clamp current returns to HGND through R607 alone: positive (6.00-3.2)/330 = 8.5 mA, negative (6.00-1.6)/330 = 13.3 mA against the 10 mA continuous input current of 6.1; 8.3.4 gives the undervoltage clamp only as "the reverse breakdown voltage" with no value, so the clamp level the arithmetic needs is not sourced, and the sheet states no pulse figure. circuit-proof.md E1.7 still reads 4.24 mA and 6.67 mA (divided by 660 ohm). Would close: the arithmetic on R607 alone with a sourced clamp level inside 10 mA, or a larger R607. |  |
| 7.10 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.9 (5.1). Nets +5V_GAUGE (JP791 pin 2, C792, J791 pin 1 to the retained gauge driver) and +5V_WB (JP761 pin 2, J761 pin 1 to the wall board) follow +5V, which the supply module over-voltage trip takes to 6.75 V (IRM-20-SPEC 2025-11-21, circuit-proof.md row "+5V over-voltage") and the cable position of JP301 takes to the 10.3 V clamp level of D402. The VID6608 sheet (Rev 1, 2022, Absolute Maximum Ratings, ds/vid-a.txt) allows VDD -0.3 to +6 V, so 6.75 V is 0.75 V over; no record gives the wall board a rating. Nothing clamps or limits either rail. Gauge drive and Heater LED drive and wall board header sheets. Owner decision: acceptance (k) names the rail over-voltage fault states, the +5V module trip and the gauge and load-cell 5 V rails (it cites findings 6.9 and 6.10), ground the regulating part failing short and the damage staying in low-voltage logic, bound a dead controller letting K201 open; it covers this finding for the module-trip excursion; it does not cover the 10.3 V cable-position excursion of the gauge driver and the wall board, because acceptance (b) names that surge only for U201 and U791 (7.0 V). |  |
| 7.11 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.10. The gauge control lines /Gauge drive/GAUGE_RST_B, GAUGE_STEP1_B, GAUGE_DIR1_B, GAUGE_DIR2_B, GAUGE_STEP2_B (J791 pins 3, 4, 5, 8, 9) and the buffer outputs GAUGE_*_Y behind R791 to R795: with JP791 open or the gauge assembly unpowered (+5V_GAUGE absent, a state bring-up-provision.md and open-items.md M17 use) U791 (powered from +5V) still drives up to 5.25 V through 100 ohm into driver inputs rated VDD + 0.3 V (VID6608 Rev 1, 2022); the sheet states no input clamp current, so the series resistor has no arithmetic against a diode current, and the back-fed current (5.25 V - 0.7 V)/100 ohm = 46 mA per line exceeds the 35 mA IO limit of U791 (SN74HCT541 SCLS306E 5.1) while C792 charges. Gauge drive sheet, U791 pins 14 to 18, J791. Owner decision: acceptance (k) cites finding 6.10 for the gauge 5 V rail, but its ground is the regulating part failing short and passing its input rail; this finding rests on a normal bring-up or service state (JP791 open, firmware running), a different ground, so (k) does not cover this finding. |  |
| 7.12 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.11. /MAINS_PRES_C and /MAINS_PRES_S (U401 PE15 and PD7, FT_h) behind R764 27 kohm with R765 82 kohm and R774 with R775: the record states an interface requirement of at most 5.5 V for the wall board (open-items.md "Wall-board levels on the mains-presence confirms"; circuit-proof.md mains-presence row), but 5.5 V x the divider ratio 0.7485 to 0.756 = 4.12 to 4.16 V at the pin, over the 4.0 V that DS12110 Rev 11 Table 109 allows with VDD absent; the record's own arithmetic uses 5.125 V (3.86 V) and no record declares what the wall board can drive. Heater LED drive and wall board header sheet. |  |
| 7.13 | PINV-1 | function | New (the sink-current part continues the record's own "no" row). /KEY1 to /KEY5 (U401 PE2 to PE6, FT_h) and /ANODE_RAIL (J791 pin 7, J821 pin 7): (a) the rail feeds the key pins through the panel indicators and must be off before VDD falls through about 1.65 V (DS12110 Table 112 operating limit min(VDD)+3.6 V, 4.0 V maximum with VDD absent); circuit-verdicts.md marks net ANODE_RAIL a FINDING (brown-out interval not bounded) and open-items.md "Brown-out timing of the anode rail" leaves the fall time to a bring-up reading with a diode clamp as the fallback; the schematic holds no such clamp. (b) circuit-proof.md row "Key line sink current" is "no": a pin sinking two indicator elements at 300 ohm each is 26.3 mA at a forward voltage of 0 V and is inside the 20 mA of DS12110 Table 12 only for a forward voltage of at least 0.95 V, which connector-pinouts.md lists as pending. Operator panel and indicators sheet, J821. |  |
| 7.14 | PINV-1 | function | Continues 6.70 (a free-pass finding of round 6; G3 reports it as G3-3, which I did not read). Nets +3V3 and /Flow, pressure and spare analogue inputs/SPAREA_3V3, BREWA_3V3, SPAN2_3V3 (J523, J524, J525 pins 1 and 2), Flow, pressure and spare analogue inputs sheet: each header puts +5V on pin 1 directly beside the 3.3 V feed on pin 2 (netlist: J523.1, J524.1, J525.1 on +5V; J523.2, J524.2, J525.2 on the feed, which runs R542 to R544 (0 ohm link) and the PTC F522 to F524 to +3V3). A cable fray, a crushed or offset plug or a solder bridge between the two adjacent pins drives +3V3 from +5V (5.125 V; 5.25 V in the record's worst case) through at least the 1.35 ohm Rmin of the PTC (Bourns MF-NSMF012 Rev V 07/17). U302 (LT1963A) can only source, so the rail rises while the injected current exceeds the load: with the 0.293 A the record gives (circuit-proof.md section B), 5.25 V x 11.3 / (11.3 + 1.35) = 4.7 V, and nearly 5.2 V at the 37.3 mA of open-items.md row 17; the PTC trips in 0.20 s at 1 A (maker), but a tripped part passes 0.4 W typical, about 0.2 A at a 2 V drop, which can still exceed a light load, so the excess can last as long as the bridge. Every 4.0 V part on the rail is over its absolute maximum: U401 VDD and VBAT (DS12110 Rev 11 Table 109), U620 and U621 (MAX31865 Rev 3 VDD and DVDD 4.0 V) and Y601 (SiT8008B Vdd 4 V). The records examine a short from the feed to GND (open-items.md, the 2.67 A, 0.2 s row) and the short-safe PTC, and no record examines this bridge. K201 (welded or stuck contact; POL_COIL_LO shorted to ground, for example at the TP205 pad or the Q202 drain, which bypasses both channels), U201 (output oscillating of itself with no input edge) and Z201 or Z202 (a shorted clamp zener with a coil inductance above 1.10 H, unmeasured: open-items.md M28) each leave the live feed to every load (K201 contact 13 to 14, LINE1) energised and are neither removed nor detected by the chain's own means; circuit-proof.md A bounds them by series thermostats and a one-shot non-restoring cutoff that are not drawn on this schematic. Owner decision: acceptance (a) of DEC-MAIN-BOARD-RESIDUAL-RISKS-ACCEPTED-BY-OWNER names the K201 weld and these three further interlock-drive faults (U201 oscillating, Z201 or Z202 short above 1.10 H, POL_COIL_LO shorted to ground), bounded by the series overheat thermostats now and the owed one-shot non-restoring cutoff (DEC-CHAIN-FAULT-BOUNDED-BY-INDEPENDENT-ELEMENT's third outcome), ground: the weld is not a hazard alone because the heaters still switch; it covers this finding, on the condition (a) states, that the cutoff is owed and not yet fitted (no part of the decision stands in for fitting it) and that the reference machine does not establish whether the thermostats reset. |  |

The record's FAULT row says a shorted diode leaves the zener 'forward across the coil, starving it: removed'. From the netlist a shorted D205 puts POL_CLAMP_1 on +5V and so Z201 (anode POL_CLAMP_1, cathode POL_COIL_LO) is forward biased from +5V into POL_COIL_LO whenever Q201 and Q202 conduct: about 4.3 V over a zener forward resistance (taken as 1.5 ohm) and 2 x 1.2 ohm of FETs is about 1 A against ID 400 mA and IDM 1.6 A for 10 us (NX3008NBK Table 5) and IF 200 mA for the BZX84 (Table 5), about 1.4 W in each FET against Ptot 350 mW, while the coil sees about 2.3 V against 3.5 V pick-up. A short before power-up leaves the relay open (safe, found at the first power-up); a short in service holds the stack in overload until a FET fails, and whether it fails open (coil released) or drain-source short (both channels bypassed, the POL_COIL_LO to ground case) is not shown by the record. Owner decision: acceptance (a) names POL_COIL_LO shorted to ground bounded by the series thermostats and the owed cutoff, but names no shorted clamp diode and no forward conduction of its series zener, so it does not cover this finding. |  |

## Change after round 7: seven like-for-like resistor swaps

- **Date**: 2026-11-06. Not a round: the review has no round 8 for this change, on the owner's decision of the same day (DEC-MAIN-BOARD-RESIDUAL-RISKS-ACCEPTED-BY-OWNER, entry (z2)), which puts these checks in its place: the netlist and parts-list comparison, the proof scripts and the deck comparison, the full pre-order check compared by rule with its baseline, and this re-judgement. Round 7's text above is not altered, and its findings table keeps its Closed by column as written.
- **The change**: R607 and R608 (Supply voltage and current measurement sheet) 330 ohm to 470 ohm; R791 to R795 (Gauge drive sheet) 100 ohm to 470 ohm. One part for all seven: UNI-ROYAL 0603WAF4700T5E, LCSC C23179, basic, 0603 `Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric`, the footprint they already had. Schematic commit 7ba6398c, board file commit aeab20b5 (21 property lines, no geometry), records and proof scripts commit e6b8d86e. U402 is not changed.
- **Netlist and parts list**: the netlist exported before and after differs in exactly the value, LCSC and MPN fields of these seven parts (R607, R608: 330, C23138, 0603WAF3300T5E; R791 to R795: 100, C22775, 0603WAF1000T5E; all now 470, C23179, 0603WAF4700T5E) and in its date and source lines, nothing else. The parts list the ordering step builds (`kicad-cli sch export bom --group-by LCSC --exclude-dnp`) shows one line `R607,R608,R791-R795 / 470 / C23179`, the 100 ohm line loses R791 to R795 and the C23138 line is gone. The placement file differs in the Val column of these seven rows only.
- **Basis of the re-judgement**: the new values and the rows added to circuit-proof.md (E1.7 rewritten on R607 alone; Gauge harness short, Gauge back-fed state and Gauge line edge rows after the Gauge buffer levels row), their scripts `E_amc_front_end.py`, `E_amc_ch1_shunt.cir` and `D_margins.py` with their logs rerun, the UNI-ROYAL thick film data sheet (0603 100 mW, 75 V; ds/g5-uniroyal-thickfilm-C25804.txt), SN74HCT541 SCLS306E (ds/sn74hct541.txt: IO +/-35 mA, VCC or GND +/-70 mA, VOH 3.84 V at -6 mA, 4.4 V at -20 uA), VID6608 Rev 1 (ds/vid-a.txt: VIH 3.15 V, VIL 1.35 V, input leakage +/-10 uA, minimum pulse 450 ns, 7.2 kHz, no input clamp current stated) and AMC131M02 SBASA56 (ds/amc131m02-sbasa56.txt: 6.1, 6.3, 6.8, 8.3.4).

"Unchanged" means the row's reasons do not depend on the changed values and its verdict stands as round 7 gave it.

### Findings

- **7.9 is closed by this change.** The arithmetic is now on R607 alone and sits 4.1 % inside 10 mA in its worst case (circuit-proof.md E1.7), which is the "a larger R607" the finding offers. Open as stated in the AMC_AIN1P row: the clamp level is the absolute-maximum 1.6 V, not a sourced figure. That is a limitation of the record's method that the maker's sheet does not answer, carried in open-items.md row 11 and in E1.7, and is not what 7.9 asked for.
- **7.62 is closed by this change.** The harness-short half (51.6 mW against 60 mW, 10.5 mA against 35 mA) is met and recorded in the Gauge harness short row, which round 7 said no record held. The cable-position half was acceptance (b)'s in round 7 and is unchanged.
- **7.11 is closed as to U791 and not as to the driver.** The U791 half is met (9.8 mA per line and 48.9 mA together against 35 mA and 70 mA) and the Gauge back-fed state row is the record round 7 found missing. The other half, that VID6608 states no input clamp current so the series resistor has no arithmetic against the driver's diode, is unchanged: it needs a maker figure, a bring-up measurement or the owner's acceptance, and this change supplies none of them. 7.11 therefore stays open for that half, and its Closed by is not written here.
- **7.82 is answered in part.** Its gauge-conductor half has its record row now (the Gauge harness short row), and acceptance (t) already covers 7.82 and names those rows as owed; the ANODE_RAIL half is unchanged.
- **Unaffected**: every other Round 7 finding, among them 7.10, 7.22, 7.30 (U402 is not changed, its carry to DEL-HW-BRING-UP.C15 under DEC-SCHEMATIC-REVIEW-FINDINGS-CARRIED-BY-OWNER stands), 7.39, 7.43, 7.61, 7.72, 7.73, 7.79.
- **New facts this change adds to the records**: C23179 is in catalogue-extract.yaml (read 2026-11-06: basic, stock 4,163,039, 0.0023 USD at 1 to 9; no lifecycle published by the sources read); C23138 is out of it, no position using it. The gauge buffer's VOH behind R806 on GAUGE_RST_B is 3.66 V against VIH 3.15 V, 0.51 V margin (round 7's figure ignored R806).
